title: Attaching audio, voices, and playlist inspiration
text: Hi, I'm Rohan from Humanitarians AI. This is part three, the last one. You can already make a song and drive the advanced panel. This video is the ring around it. What you can bring into a track and what you can do with one once you have it. Here is the whole idea. Everything left sits on one of two sides of the panel you already know. On the way in, three buttons let you attach

title: Sounds tab: Generating short samples and loops
text: Your own material. On the way out, a menu on every track decides what happens next. Both ends return to the same advanced panel. Above the lyrics box sit three buttons. Add audio takes a file, browse, upload, or record straight in.

title: Remixing vs editing your tracks

title: Mastering the Extend tool
text: Sample or upload one and Sunno uses it to shape how your songs sing. Four things matter. Sing in the style you want. Record at least 10 seconds. Find a quiet spot and a decent microphone helps, though your laptop will do. The third tab is sounds. And it does not make songs. It makes short samples,

title: Pro exports: WAVs, stems, and videos
text: Effects, loops, and oneshots. One field describes the sound you want. Its own advanced options hold three controls. type either a oneshot or a loop then BPM and key both of which you can leave on automatic. Now the other side every track carries a three dot menu and it is where everything after generation lives. 10 entries split down the middle. Five open a submen, remix, edit, share, download and manage. The other five act at once, publish it, cue it, add it to a playlist, start a radio station, or send it to the trash. Remix and edit look alike and are not. Remix makes a new song from this one, a cover in another genre, a mashup, a sample. Edit changes this

Song. Extend it, crop it, remove a section, reverse it, slow it down, and picking either does the same thing. It reopens the advanced panel with your track attached. Extend is the one you will reach for most, and it is worth seeing properly. Your track loads into the panel as attached audio with the mode set to extend. The waveform splits in two. The part you keep and the part suno recreates. Drag the boundary to say where the new material starts. Then press create. Last getting it out. Download opens four choices. MP3 is the plain one and needs nothing extra. That is the file you hand in. WAV gives you a lossless master. Get stems splits the track into its individual parts and

Video renders it for posting. Those three carry a pro badge. the whole series in one place. Sign in with Discord. Describe a song in simple mode and let it run. Move to advanced when the words matter. Attach audio, a voice, or a playlist when you want your own material in it. Then use the track menu to extend, remix, or download what you made. That is the whole tool. Across three videos, you have gone from never having used SUO to signing in, writing a description on purpose, driving every control in the advanced panel, and getting a finished file out. Everything after this is practice. Make something for your project this week and keep the ones that surprise you. Rohan vijjkumar humanitarians AI
